Bloomberg reported yesterday that Apple is partnering with LG to develop new smart home accessories, which will launch under the LG brand, with leaked images revealing the design of a smart door lock, thermostat and temperature sensor.

Images reveal the three Home accessories Apple reportedly developed for LG

Next week, Apple is rumoured to be unveiling a long-awaited major update to its Home lineup. The company is bringing a brand-new Apple TV 4K and HomePod mini, as well as an entirely new product category we've been calling 'HomePad'.

However, yesterday's Bloomberg report revealed another piece of Apple's Home product strategy. The company has partnered with LG to develop new Home accessories, which will be sold under the LG brand.

According to the report, these accessories include a smart door lock, thermostat, temperature sensor, video doorbell, indoor camera, outdoor camera and floodlight camera.

Today, leaker pdfu shared the first images of three of those products: the smart door lock, smart thermostat and temperature sensor.

Popular posts from LateStage

LG, isn't that the TV brand that was caught spying on users even after the power was turned off? Where has Apple's commitment to privacy gone?

pdfu also revealed more details about the products in a thread of posts on X.

For example, the smart deadbolt features a rotating keypad with a 'ring of lights on the touchpad, audio alert when the door isn't closed, sound volume for the lock,' and supports auto-unlock among other features.

Mark Gurman has noted that these new products may not ship in time for the rollout of Apple's new HomePod and Apple TV. However, there's still a good chance Apple will mention them at next week's event.

What do you think of these smart home accessories designed by Apple and sold under the LG brand? Share your thoughts in the comments.
